title.zh: 原子氢1s辐射复合速率系数

summary: Evaluate the H+ + e -> H(1s) + hv analytic rate coefficient from electron temperature in eV.

capability: Analytic H+ + e -> H(1s) + hv rate coefficient evaluated from electron temperature in eV.
operation: Evaluate the H+ + e -> H(1s) radiative recombination rate coefficient
electron temperature in eV -> rate coefficient in m^3/s
discovery.model: Level-1 Storey-type analytic fit with fixed constants; no external-data interpolation or runtime cross-section integral.
discovery.geometry: None; pointwise scalar or array material samples with no spatial axis inferred (coordinate: electron temperature in eV).
discovery.boundary: Temperature must be finite and strictly positive; out-of-range values clip to the fit endpoints and the represented output must be finite and positive.

identity.relation: H+ + e -> H(1s) + hv radiative recombination rate coefficient as a function of electron temperature
identity.direction: electron temperature in eV -> rate coefficient in m^3/s
identity.definition: Clip strictly positive electron temperature to [0.1, 2.01e4] eV. With Ry=13.58 eV, n=1, A_nl=3.92 and x_nl=0.35, set ionization_energy=Ry/n and b_n=ionization_energy/T. Return A_nl*1e-14*sqrt(ionization_energy/Ry)*(b_n^1.5/(b_n+x_nl))*1e-6 m^3/s in the declared arithmetic order.
identity.model: level-1 Storey-type analytic fit with fixed constants; no external-data interpolation or runtime cross-section integral
identity.geometry: none; pointwise scalar or array material samples
identity.coordinates: electron temperature in eV, with no spatial axis inferred
identity.boundary: finite real numeric temperature strictly positive; endpoint clipping; finite positive represented output
assumptions: The Ry=13.58 eV, A_nl=3.92, x_nl=0.35 and n=1 constants and the arithmetic order define the fit on finite positive real inputs.
Only ground-state H(1s) radiative recombination is represented; excited levels and other recombination mechanisms are separate relations.
This callable rejects nonpositive temperature and does not coerce boolean or numeric-string inputs; the declared positive real input contract is the only accepted domain.

inputs.name: electron_temperature_ev
inputs.description: Electron temperature for the H(1s) radiative recombination fit.
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; positive values outside [0.1, 2.01e4] eV are clipped to the nearest endpoint.

outputs.name: rate_m3_s
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive on accepted inputs; no external physical accuracy is asserted.

preconditions: The caller supplies electron temperature in eV and accepts endpoint clipping.
Above 30 eV the caller accepts a low-biased value: the fit is validated only on [0.1, 30] eV and warns outside it.
Below 0.1 eV the caller accepts the 0.1 eV endpoint value, which understates the true rate and warns.
supported: Scalar and array evaluation of the H(1s) analytic fit on [0.1, 30] eV. The fit's accuracy there is a 5.75% envelope: the observed worst departure from an independent Stobbe-Milne oracle is 5.72% at about 19.5 eV on a 601-point log grid, so 5.75% bounds the sampled interval rather than describing a measured precision.
excluded: Excited-level, three-body and dielectronic recombination, or electron-impact ionization.
A physically validated recombination model outside the compared domain or without an external atomic-physics reference.

Qualified use above 30 eV: the fit understates the true rate (about 37% at 1 keV, a factor of about 2.0-2.1 at 10-20 keV); those samples return the fit's own value at their temperature with a warning.
Qualified use below 0.1 eV: the 0.1 eV endpoint value is returned and understates the true rate (about 3.4x low at 0.01 eV); a warning is emitted.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-real numeric, non-finite or nonpositive electron temperature. Boolean, complex and numeric-string coercions are rejected.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the derived rate is non-finite or nonpositive; no partial output is returned. Emits scirel.ApplicabilityWarning when any input temperature is above 30 eV (the validated upper limit) or below 0.1 eV (the fit's lower limit); those samples return the value at the corresponding fit-interval endpoint or the fit's own value, never a silent truncation.

example.description: Evaluate ground-state recombination inside and outside the validated interval.
example.code:
import warnings
import numpy as np
import scirel
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_1s_radiative_recombination_rate
t = np.array([0.1, 1.0, 50000.0])
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    r = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_1s_radiative_recombination_rate(t)
assert r.shape == (3,) and np.all(np.isfinite(r)) and np.all(r > 0.0)
# the 50000 eV sample is above the validated limit: one warning, value still returned
assert len(caught) == 1 and issubclass(caught[0].category, scirel.ApplicabilityWarning)
edge = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_1s_radiative_recombination_rate(np.array([0.1, 1.0]))
np.testing.assert_array_equal(r[:2], edge)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as low:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    clipped = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_1s_radiative_recombination_rate(
        np.array([0.01, 20100.0])
    )
# both ends clip to their interval endpoint, and both announced themselves
assert len(low) == 2 and np.all(clipped > 0.0)
example.expected: Three positive H(1s) rates; in-range samples equal the fit, out-of-range samples clip to the interval endpoint and emit one ApplicabilityWarning each call.

scope: Six fixed reference values and an independent closed-form evaluation hold to a 1e-15 relative tolerance, including on a holdout grid.
Direct tests cover monotonic temperature dependence on the sampled grid, clipping, scalar shape, invalid domain and non-real input rejection.

No external implementation comparison is maintained or replayed by this repository; the maintained tests validate the declared relation against an in-repository independent formulation and cover the stated rejection and clipping behaviour only on their tested grids.
Low- and high-temperature logarithmic slopes converge to the analytic -1/2 and -3/2 asymptotic limits within the audited temperature windows.

Against an independent Stobbe-Milne oracle (Stobbe 1930 photoionization closed form plus the Milne relation with g_n/g_+ = 2, no fit input), the observed worst departure on a 601-point log grid over [0.1, 30] eV is 5.72% at about 19.5 eV; the anchor ratios at 0.1, 1, 10, 20 and 30 eV are 0.9473085930, 0.9647996863, 1.0432707998, 1.0571517077 and 1.0490534031, and the oracle gives 1.581929e-13 cm^3/s at 1e4 K.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The tests establish the discrete fit, clipping and failure contract on tested samples and bound its accuracy on [0.1, 30] eV against a physics-only oracle (observed maximum 5.72% on the tested grid, not a proven continuous bound). The printed literature table was not re-verified in this round. Public distribution licensing remains pending.
known_limitations: No external physical-reference oracle is bound; this gap remains open.
Ry=13.58 eV is the fit constant and is not replaced with a modern re-derived value.
Out-of-fit-range positive temperatures silently repeat endpoint rates.
No environment-gated external-implementation comparison exists in this repository; any earlier external comparison is not replayed by the maintained tests.
The declared 5.75% accuracy is an observed maximum on a 601-point log grid, not a proof of a continuous upper bound; the earlier 5.3% claim was refuted by the 20 eV point (+5.715%).
The oracle agrees with the commonly quoted alpha_1 = 1.58e-13 cm^3/s at 1e4 K, but the printed table behind that number was not re-checked; treat the literature comparison as UNKNOWN until it is.
